1) <strong>Who are you, and what do you do?</strong>

I am the grandson of
<a href="http://people.few.eur.nl/wakker/miscella/private/myphotos/myfamily/myroots.jpg">http://people.few.eur.nl/wakker/miscella/private/myphotos/myfamily/myroots.jpg</a>

I will convert all of mankind, including all statisticians, to Bayesianism.
I will introduce the idea of conservation of influence.

2) <strong>What do you consider your most important research tool(s) on your computer?</strong>  Delete-key.

3) <strong>What do you consider your most important research tool(s) outside of your computer?</strong>
Paper-shredder.

4)  <strong>What is your favorite tip for getting writing done?
</strong>Do not force yourself to write; it will not work.
Only forbid yourself to do anything other than writing.

<a href="http://people.few.eur.nl/wakker/index.html">Peter's CV</a>

The best paper that I ever co-authored was
Abdellaoui, Mohammed &amp; Peter P. Wakker (2005). T<a href="http://doi.org/10.1007/s11238-005-8320-4">he Likelihood Method for Decision under Uncertainty</a>. <em>Theory and Decision, 58</em>, 3–76.

It is also my least-cited paper. Explanation (to console myself): In those days the journal printed half per page what other journals did.  In another journal the paper would have taken 37 pages not 74.  No-one prints 74 pages for one paper.
